newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Polysindo starts new plants.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Polysindo starts new plants.

text.p: Indonesia's largest polyester producer PT Polysindo Eka Perkasa on Friday commissioned new purified terephthalic acid (PTA) and polymer plants, which will enable it to produce 360,000 tonnes of PTA annually.
The plants, which are part of the company's $645 million expansion programme and located in Karawang, West Java, were inaugurated by President Suharto.
Polysindo is a unit of the Texmaco Group conglomerate, which also has interests in textile machinery and textile products.
Before the completion of the facilities, the company had to buy PTA, a main ingredient for polyester chips, from Bakrie & Brothers and state-owned oil company Pertamina.
Bakrie produces 500,000 tonnes of PTA annually.
"These plants will produce raw material for the textile industry which is the main backbone of Indonesia's non-oil exports," Suharto said in his speech.

Polysindo said in a statement that upon the completion of the current expansion programme by the fourth quarter of 1997, Polysindo's annual capacity will total 360,000 tonnes of PTA, 330,000 tonnes of polymer and 187,000 tonnes of staple fibre. It gave no further details.

Polysindo's president director Marimutu Sinivasan said the reason behind the expansion programme was to trim foreign exchange outflows needed to import costly capital goods and equipment for the textiles industry.

"One of my goals in vertically integrating the polyester business and building an engineering company in Indonesia is to break that cycle and give Indonesia blocks of industry right here within our borders," he said.

Polysindo's posted a net profit of 169.8 billion rupiah in 1996 compared with 210.97 billion rupiah the previous year, but the 1995 figure included a one-time gain from the sale of a subsidiary. ($1 = 2,438 rupiah) -- Jakarta Newsroom + 6221 384-6364
